great.name: Built-in SI Buffer
great.quote: (9) Super Reload: What is covered We shall provide for a Reload of the Sum Insured, unlimited times during the Policy Year... (ii) The Super Reload of Sum Insured shall apply to the ﬁrst claim in the Policy Year. (iii) ... available ... to any Illness / Injury (including its complications) for which a claim has been admitted...
great.explanation: The policy provides unlimited super reloads of the sum insured during the policy year, even for the same illness or its complications. This means your coverage can increase beyond the base sum insured for multiple or high-value claims.

great.name: Restore Benefit
great.quote: (8) Reload of Sum Insured: ... Once in the Policy Year, We shall provide for a reload of the Sum Insured...; (9) Super Reload: ... Reload ... unlimited times during the Policy Year...
great.explanation: The policy includes both reload and super reload benefits that replenish your sum insured during the policy year. This ensures extra coverage is available after claims, enhancing your financial protection.

great.name: Bariatric Surgery
great.quote: (12) Obesity Treatment: What is Covered We shall cover the related Medical Expenses... if the Insured Person is hospitalized for a Bariatric Surgery which is medically necessary...
great.explanation: Medically necessary bariatric surgery is covered under the policy, subject to medical criteria and approval. This is helpful since many base policies exclude obesity-related surgeries.

good.name: Initial Waiting Period
good.quote: 3. 30-day waiting period (Code- Excl03) ... Expenses related to the treatment of any illness within 30 days from the ﬁrst policy commencement date shall be excluded except claims arising due to an accident...
good.explanation: There is a standard 30-day waiting period for illnesses, but accidents are covered from day one. This is a common industry practice.

good.name: Specific Illness Waiting
good.quote: 2. Speciﬁed disease / procedure waiting period: (Code- Excl02) ... shall be excluded until the expiry of 24 months of continuous coverage after the date of inception...
good.explanation: Specified diseases and procedures are covered after a 24-month waiting period, which aligns with typical market standards.

good.name: Domiciliary Hospitalization
good.quote: (5) Domiciliary Hospitalisation: What is covered We shall cover the Medical Expenses incurred for the Insured Person’s Domiciliary Hospitalization...
good.explanation: Home-based treatment when hospitalization is not possible or a bed is unavailable is covered, subject to policy terms.

good.name: Air Ambulance
good.quote: (15) Domestic Emergency Assistance Services (including Air Ambulance)... (16) International Emergency Assistance Services (including Air Ambulance)...
good.explanation: Emergency evacuation and air ambulance services are included for domestic and international travel, subject to conditions and service rules.

bad.name: Room Rent
bad.quote: (i) Reasonable and Customary Charges for Room Rent ... up to the limits as speciﬁed in the Policy Schedule / Product Beneﬁt Table of this Policy; (ii) If the Insured Person is admitted in a room category / limit that is higher than the one that is speciﬁed ... then the Insured Person shall bear a rateable proportion of the Room Rent (and the total Associated Medical Expenses...)
bad.reference: Section C.I.(1) In-patient Hospitalization (What is covered & Conditions)
bad.explanation: Room rent is limited to specified categories in the policy schedule, and choosing a higher room category leads to proportional deduction of room rent and related expenses. This can increase your out-of-pocket costs.

bad.name: Disease Sub-limits

bad.explanation: Certain treatments have fixed payout caps which may be much lower than actual costs, potentially causing significant out-of-pocket expenses.
